title: A right-grouped predicate chain
gloss: I like all cats. Word for word, I like the set of all cats.
hint: An Eberban chain groups from the right: tcu mian forms the set of all cats, and dona links mi to that set.

title: Choose who receives an apple
text: mi duna vo mo vei meon
hint: The words vo mo name the recipient. The closer vei returns to the main chain.

title: Leave the final closer unwritten
text: duna ve mi fo mo fa meon
hint: Replace [+VEI] with VEI in bind-group to require the final closing word.

title: Words without spaces
hint: The dots mark pauses before ualis and eberban, and after ualis. The forms stage finds five words without spaces.

title: Join two actions
text: mi pe etiansa bu dona pei meon
gloss: I eat and like an apple.
hint: The words pe and pei group the actions. The word bu separates them.

title: Compounds, grammatical quotes and foreign quotes
text: a ca mi dona eberban cai siro co [I like Eberban]
gloss: The Eberban text "mi dona eberban" has the translation "I like Eberban".
hint: The forms stage reads the compound eberban and the foreign quote co [...] as single tokens, while syntax parses ca ... cai.

title: Spell a name
text: za ce bu o bu tco cei
hint: Each unit inside ce and cei spells one character. The unit tco spells the digit 3.

title: Count cats with a digit
hint: The digit 2 becomes ta. The word ji makes the number count things.

title: Resuming the deepest matching verb with pa
text: a mi jveo per jveo gour pa jveo va bjan
gloss: I am a friend of a person who is a friend of a beautiful dog.
hint: The particle pa resumes the latest matching jveo in the chain. Remove the fewest #·passed-step step from %ambiguity-resolution to see a tie.

title: Erasing sentences with ra and chains with ri
text: a mi pban ra a mi dona meon ri mi dona mian
gloss: I like a cat. The erased words are a faulty sentence and a chain that says "I like an apple".
hint: The particle ra erases the faulty sentence a mi pban with its consonant error, and ri restarts the chain after a.

title: An accepted text with a hyphen warning
text: a mi dona tcu mian bja-n
hint: Eberban allows hyphens at syllable boundaries and warns on bja-n before a final consonant. Set hyphen-misplaced to Off in Options to hide the warning.

title: Explain an unfinished binding
gloss: Intended: I give you an apple. The text stops after the word vo.
hint: The recipient is missing after vo. Add mo vei meon to say "I give you an apple."

title: A voicing fault inside a root
gloss: The text has no full meaning. It reads "I like" and then pban, which is not a valid word.
hint: The forms stage marks pb with %error and hands the word on, so syntax builds a complete tree and reports pb.

title: After ra, a sentence needs its starter
text: a mi dona tcu mian ra mo dona tcu gour
gloss: Intended: You like all dogs. The erased sentence says "I like all cats".
hint: The message comes from the %error clause of this rule. Write a before mo to correct the text.

title: A free prefix before a number
text: a mi bure di 3 ji meon
gloss: Intended: I eat three apples, with the attention on the number.
hint: A number takes no free prefix such as di, and no %error rule covers this position, so syntax rejects the text.
